                        1          Plaintiff Phil, Inc. files this Complaint against Defendant DGN Pharmacy, Inc. d/b/a

                        2   PersonalRx and alleges as follows:

                        3                                     NATURE OF THE ACTION

                        4          1.      This is a breach of contract action for PersonalRx to make good on its promise to

                        5   pay Phil for prescription medicine that Phil and its affiliate, Western Wellness Solutions, Inc.

                        6   provided to PersonalRx.

                        7          2.      Phil and PersonalRx signed a contract where Phil directs prescriptions to PersonalRx

                        8   to review and fill. Under the contract, PersonalRx may buy product from Phil and Western

                        9   Wellness to fill prescriptions.

                       10          3.      For months, PersonalRx got the value of the bargain, as Phil directed hundreds of

                       11   patients with thousands of prescriptions to PersonalRx. Phil and Western Wellness provided

                       12   PersonalRx the product to dispense. All that PersonalRx had to do was pay Phil and Western
F ENWICK & W EST LLP




                       13   Wellness back. But PersonalRx has refused, accumulating millions of dollars in unpaid invoices.

                       14   Phil brings this action to hold PersonalRx to the straightforward terms of the contract it signed.

                       15                                             THE PARTIES

                       16          4.      Phil is a corporation organized under the laws of Delaware, with a principal place

                       17   of business at 14500 N. Northsight Blvd, Suite 307, Scottsdale, Arizona. Phil is a platform that

                       18   connects pharmaceutical manufacturers, healthcare providers, and patients to streamline the

                       19   prescription fulfillment process. Phil offers an end-to-end system to transmit prescriptions directly

                       20   to a nationwide network of partner pharmacies, while facilitating prior authorization, insurance

                       21   benefit verification, and patient onboarding. Phil’s platform reduces administrative burdens for

                       22   healthcare providers, shortens time-to-therapy for patients, and helps manufacturers improve

                       23   adherence and outcomes for their therapies.

                       24          5.      PersonalRx is a corporation organized under the laws of New Jersey with a principal

                       25   place of business at 20 Murray Hill Parkway, Suite 210 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. PersonalRx

                       26   is a pharmacy that contracted with Phil to dispense prescriptions to patients through Phil’s platform.

                       27

                       28

                            COMPLAINT                                                                       Case No. 3:26-cv-504
                              Case 4:26-cv-00504-YGR            Document 1         Filed 01/16/26     Page 3 of 7



                        1                                     JURISDICTION AND VENUE
                        2           6.       This Court has subject matter jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1332 as no defendant

                        3   in this action is a resident of the same state as the plaintiff, and the amount in controversy exceeds

                        4   $75,000.

                        5           7.       This Court has personal jurisdiction over PersonalRx because PersonalRx agreed

                        6   that Phil can bring this action to collect on debts in any court in any jurisdiction; committed and/or

                        7   contributed to the commission of the unlawful acts in this judicial district described in this

                        8   Complaint; registered for and engaged in business activities in and directed to this judicial district;

                        9   and otherwise purposely availed itself of the privileges and benefits of the laws of the State of

                       10   California.

                       11           8.       Venue is proper in this judicial district under 28 U.S.C. § 1391 because PersonalRx

                       12   breached the contract by failing to pay invoices issued in this district. PersonalRx has targeted
F ENWICK & W EST LLP




                       13   sales to California residents in this district at least by operating a fully interactive commercial

                       14   website, https://personalrx.com, offering prescriptions for sale to California residents in this

                       15   district. PersonalRx committed unlawful acts in this district and wrongfully caused Phil substantial

                       16   injury in this district.

                       17                                     DIVISIONAL ASSIGNMENT
                       18           9.       Events giving rise to this action occurred in Alameda County. PersonalRx breached

                       19   the contract at issue by failing to pay invoices issued in San Leandro, California.

                       20                         PHIL’S INNOVATIVE PRESCRIPTION PLATFORM
                       21           10.      A patient’s journey to consume prescription drugs is often too complicated. The

                       22   patient first must consult a provider. If the provider writes a prescription, the patient needs to find

                       23   a pharmacy to dispense the drug. After the patient chooses a pharmacy, the provider needs to

                       24   transfer the patient’s prescription information to the pharmacy. The pharmacy needs to review the

                       25   information and check whether the patient’s insurance will cover the drug. Often times for non-

                       26   generic drugs, the insurer will require the patient’s provider to submit a Prior Authorization to

                       27   approve coverage. After the Prior Authorization is submitted, the pharmacy then must figure out

                       28   if coverage has been approved, what portion of the cost the insurer will cover, and what to charge

                            COMPLAINT                                         3                               Case No. 3:26-cv-504
                              Case 4:26-cv-00504-YGR           Document 1          Filed 01/16/26    Page 4 of 7



                        1   the patient based on their plan copay and deductible. Only then can the pharmacy dispense the
                        2   prescription to the patient, assuming the patient agrees to pay the resulting out of pocket costs. And
                        3   even if the patient gets the first prescription, pharmacies may need to cycle through these steps
                        4   again throughout the patient’s therapy. Filling a prescription is an administrative labyrinth for
                        5   providers, patients, pharmacies, insurers, and pharmaceutical companies.
                        6             11.   Phil was founded in 2015 by Dr. Deepak Thomas, who saw major gaps in
                        7   prescription access and adherence. After Dr. Thomas was diagnosed with a chronic illness, he lost
                        8   time and money trying to navigate his own care, often calling doctors and insurers during lunch
                        9   breaks and paying for care out of pocket while waiting for insurance to kick in. Dr. Thomas had a
                       10   vision to create a compliant platform that connected physicians, pharmacies, and patients to reduce
                       11   delays from insurance approvals, broken communication channels, and administrative morass.
                       12             12.   Phil simplifies the prescription process through one digital hub. For patients, Phil
F ENWICK & W EST LLP




                       13   offers an e-commerce-like enrollment process to submit insurance information and obtain an
                       14   insurance coverage determination, and a pharmacy network integrated with insurers to easily find
                       15   a pharmacy that can dispense the drug, often via mail. For providers, Phil provides a seamless
                       16   prescription and Prior Authorization process to write the prescription, submit to the patient’s
                       17   insurer, and coordinate the sharing of that information with dispensing pharmacies.               For
                       18   pharmacies, Phil automates many laborious workstreams like prior authorization determinations,
                       19   refill reminders, and patient inquiries. And for pharmaceutical companies, Phil ensures that eligible
                       20   patients gain better access to care, while providing prescription lifecycle data to improve patient
                       21   adherence and outcomes. Phil’s hub allows each link in the prescription chain to communicate
                       22   better.
                       23             PHIL AND PERSONALRX’S CONTRACT AND PERSONALRX’S BREACH
                       24             13.   PersonalRx is an online pharmacy. In 2024, PersonalRx chose to join Phil’s
                       25   platform. The parties entered into a Service and Product Acquisition Agreement (the “Services
                       26   Agreement”), effective September 24, 2024. Phil signed this agreement in California.
                       27

                       28

                            COMPLAINT                                         4                              Case No. 3:26-cv-504
                              Case 4:26-cv-00504-YGR            Document 1         Filed 01/16/26     Page 5 of 7



                        1          14.     Among other things in the Services Agreement, PersonalRx agreed to promptly
                        2   process all prescriptions that it received through Phil’s platform. PersonalRx agreed to bill and
                        3   collect from patients’ insurance companies for those prescriptions.
                        4          15.     Phil offered wholesale drug sales to PersonalRx through Phil’s affiliate, Western
                        5   Wellness. PersonalRx agreed to pay for those wholesale purchases from Western Wellness.
                        6   Western Wellness is headquartered in San Leandro, California.
                        7          16.     PersonalRx guaranteed its liabilities to Phil from the Services Agreement with
                        8   PersonalRx’s own personal property, including any business accounts, inventory, and equipment.
                        9   PersonalRx also agreed to other remedies if it breached the Services Agreement, including (a) a 3
                       10   percent interest charge on any monthly balances owed to Phil and delinquent for more than 15 days,
                       11   and (b) attorneys’ fees and costs Phil incurs to collect amounts PersonalRx owes.
                       12          17.     Phil began directing patients to PersonalRx, and PersonalRx began dispensing
F ENWICK & W EST LLP




                       13   prescriptions to them. In about six months, Phil connected hundreds of patients to PersonalRx,
                       14   who filled thousands of prescriptions for them. Phil satisfied its obligations in the Services
                       15   Agreement.
                       16          18.     PersonalRx did not. PersonalRx started placing orders with Western Wellness
                       17   almost every day. Some orders approached $100,000. Western Wellness issued timely invoices to
                       18   PersonalRx for these orders.
                       19          19.     PersonalRx did not pay these invoices. From January to March 2025, PersonalRx
                       20   amassed over $2 million in unpaid invoices. To date, PersonalRx has not paid its outstanding debts
                       21   as required by the Service Agreement. For months, Phil tried to work with PersonalRx to develop
                       22   a plan for PersonalRx to repay its outstanding debt and for the parties to continue their relationship.
                       23   PersonalRx refuses and has no viable plan to satisfy what it owes. In the Service Agreement,
                       24   PersonalRx agreed that Phil may bring an action to collect money that PersonalRx owes from that
                       25   agreement. PersonalRx left Phil with no other choice than filing this complaint.
                       26

                       27

                       28

                            COMPLAINT                                         5                               Case No. 3:26-cv-504
                              Case 4:26-cv-00504-YGR              Document 1       Filed 01/16/26   Page 6 of 7



                        1                                        FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION
                        2                                        BREACH OF CONTRACT
                        3          20.     Phil incorporates by reference its allegations contained in the preceding paragraphs.

                        4          21.     On or about September 24, 2024, PersonalRx entered into a valid contract with Phil:

                        5   the Services Agreement.

                        6          22.     Under the Services Agreement, PersonalRx agreed to pay the invoices for

                        7   prescription drugs purchased under the Service Agreement.

                        8          23.     Western Wellness issued invoices to PersonalRx. PersonalRx has not paid each

                        9   invoice. PersonalRx materially breached the Services Agreement by failing to pay these invoices.

                       10          24.     As a direct and proximate result of PersonalRx’s breach, Phil has been damaged in

                       11   an amount to be determined at trial.

                       12          25.     As a direct and foreseeable result of PersonalRx’s breach, Phil has suffered and will
F ENWICK & W EST LLP




                       13   continue to suffer financial harm.

                       14          26.     Phil fulfilled all duties it owes under the Services Agreement and has not breached

                       15   the Services Agreement.

                       16
                                                                   PRAYER FOR RELIEF
                       17
                                   WHEREFORE, Phil prays for the following relief:
                       18
                                               a. A judgment that PersonalRx breached the Service Agreement under the
                       19
                                                  cause of action asserted in this Complaint;
                       20
                                               b. A judgment requiring that PersonalRx pay Phil all its damages caused by
                       21
                                                  PersonalRx’s unlawful acts, with prejudgment and post-judgment interest,
                       22
                                                  as well as post-trial damages for any ongoing breach;
                       23
                                               c. A judgment requiring that PersonalRx pay Phil nominal damages for
                       24
                                                  PersonalRx’s breach;
                       25
                                               d. A judgment awarding Phil its reasonable attorneys’ fees, costs,
                       26
                                                  disbursements, and interest, as provided by law and the Services Agreement;
                       27
                                                  and
                       28

                            COMPLAINT                                         6                             Case No. 3:26-cv-504
                              Case 4:26-cv-00504-YGR            Document 1         Filed 01/16/26      Page 7 of 7



                        1                        e. Such other relief as the Court deems just and appropriate.
                        2                                     DEMAND FOR JURY TRIAL
                        3            Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 38, Phil hereby demands a jury trial as to all
                        4   issues so triable.
                        5
